tasks.description: Use `Path.cwd()` to get the current directory. Print it and its parent.
tasks.hint:
`from pathlib import Path`
`p = Path.cwd()` returns the current working directory as a Path object.
`p.parent` gives the parent directory — Path objects support `/` for joining too.
tasks.solution:
from pathlib import Path

current = Path.cwd()
print(current)
print(current.parent)
tasks.walkthrough:
`Path.cwd()` returns the current working directory as a Path object.
`.parent` is the folder that contains it. In this app the current folder is the workspace, so the parent is `src`.

tasks.description: Create a Path object for 'myfile.txt'. Check if it exists. Write text to it and read it back.
tasks.hint:
`p = Path('myfile.txt')` — this doesn't create the file, just a path object.
`p.exists()` returns True/False.
`p.write_text('Hello!')` writes to the file; `p.read_text()` reads it back.
tasks.solution:
from pathlib import Path

p = Path('myfile.txt')
print(f'Exists before: {p.exists()}')

p.write_text('Hello from pathlib!')
print(f'Exists after: {p.exists()}')
print(p.read_text())
tasks.walkthrough:
The Path object is just a description until `write_text` creates the file.
`read_text` returns the whole contents as a string, no `open` or `with` required.

tasks.description: Use Path to build a path from parts: join 'home', 'user', 'documents', 'notes.txt'. Print the full path.
tasks.hint:
Path supports the `/` operator for joining: `Path('home') / 'user' / 'documents' / 'notes.txt'`
This is cross-platform — no need to worry about `\` vs `/`.
`str(path)` converts it to a string if needed.
tasks.solution:
from pathlib import Path

full = Path('home') / 'user' / 'documents' / 'notes.txt'
print(full)
tasks.walkthrough: Each `/` joins another part. The separator in the printed result matches the operating system, a backslash on Windows.

tasks.description: Use `Path.glob()` to list all `.json` files in the current directory.
tasks.hint:
`Path('.').glob('*.json')` returns a generator of matching Path objects.
`list(Path('.').glob('*.json'))` collects them.
For recursive search: `Path('.').rglob('*.json')` — searches subdirectories too.
tasks.solution:
from pathlib import Path

Path('sample1.json').write_text('{}')
Path('sample2.json').write_text('[]')

for p in sorted(Path('.').glob('*.json')):
    print(p.name)
tasks.walkthrough:
Two small JSON files are created first so there's something to find.
`glob('*.json')` matches any file ending in .json in the current folder. `sorted` puts the results in a stable order.

tasks.description: Use pathlib to: get the stem (filename without extension), suffix (extension), and parent of 'data/results/output.csv'.
tasks.hint:
`p = Path('data/results/output.csv')`
`p.stem` → `'output'` (filename without extension)
`p.suffix` → `'.csv'` (the extension with dot)
`p.parent` → `Path('data/results')`
tasks.solution:
from pathlib import Path

p = Path('data/results/output.csv')
print(f'stem:   {p.stem}')
print(f'suffix: {p.suffix}')
print(f'parent: {p.parent}')
tasks.walkthrough:
None of this touches the disk; the path doesn't need to exist.
`stem` drops the extension, `suffix` keeps only the extension, `parent` drops the file name.

lesson.intro:
Paths as strings are fiddly: joining with the right slash, pulling off the
extension, checking existence. `pathlib` gives you a `Path` object that
does all of that with methods, and works the same on Windows and everything
else.

sections.heading: Making and joining paths
sections.body:
`Path('...')` creates a path object; it doesn't touch the disk. The `/`
operator joins parts, using the right separator for the system.
sections.code:
from pathlib import Path

p = Path('home') / 'user' / 'documents' / 'notes.txt'
print(p)
print(p.name)
print(p.parent)

sections.heading: Taking a path apart
sections.body:
`.stem` is the file name without extension, `.suffix` is the extension,
`.parent` is the folder, `.parts` is everything as a tuple.
sections.code:
from pathlib import Path

p = Path('data/results/output.csv')
print(p.stem)
print(p.suffix)
print(p.parent)
print(p.parts)

sections.heading: Reading and writing in one call
sections.body:
`write_text` and `read_text` open, do the job, and close for you. For
small files they replace the `with open` dance.
sections.code:
from pathlib import Path

p = Path('myfile.txt')
print(p.exists())
p.write_text('Hello from pathlib')
print(p.exists())
print(p.read_text())

sections.heading: Finding files with glob
sections.code:
from pathlib import Path

print(Path.cwd().name)
for p in sorted(Path('.').glob('*.txt')):
    print(p.name)

watch_out: Creating a Path doesn't create a file. `p.exists()` is False until you write to it.
`glob` returns a generator. Wrap in `list()` or `sorted()` to see the results or use them twice.
Some functions still want strings; `str(p)` converts a Path.
